title: Single Fourier coefficient estimation bound
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the Boolean cube, and let $\\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of $[n]$. Let the accuracy and confidence parameters each be rational numbers in $(0,1/2]$, and choose any $S\\in\\mathcal F$. Draw uniformly an array of independent Boolean-cube inputs indexed by $\\mathcal F$ and by the estimator's sample indices, whose sample count is determined by those accuracy and confidence parameters. The probability that the empirical Fourier coefficient at $S$ differs from the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ by at least the accuracy parameter is at most the confidence parameter.
hypotheses_covered: target is a sign-valued Boolean-cube function
$\\mathcal F$ is a finite family of subsets of $[n]$
accuracy and confidence belong to $(0,1/2]\\cap\\mathbb Q$
